An inner ball about 0 makes every cut in a sufficiently small threshold neighborhood proper. At any such limiting cut the relative boundary is null in the cutting plane. If a slice-relative-interior point belonged to the boundary of K, a supporting hyperplane there would annihilate every slice-plane tangent direction and thus equal the cutting plane, contradicting properness. Consequently the translated indicators stabilize at interior slice points and at points outside the closed K as s tends to the limiting threshold. The common bounded orthogonal projection dominates them. This proves continuity of A_i on the neighborhood by dominated convergence and the fundamental theorem of calculus gives the two-sided continuous derivative F_i'(b)=-A_i(b), in particular F_i'(0)=-S_i.

The approved bump lemma gives one uniform positive shell margin for small signed t, preserving the exact formula F_i(b)+e_i ΔV(t) for small b and the original section data. The independent original review checked the central maximal-depth claim and the single-plane crossing in the global-curvature case. Their proof is unchanged.

The exact equalization system is C¹ because the fixed-body cap function and ΔV(t) are C¹. The rows (-S_i u_iᵀ,-1) form an invertible Jacobian by the theta-weighted sum and spanning. Implicit differentiation yields q'(0)=W V'_0, and the quotient rule yields the stated normalized derivative. For each x in all of R^d, at least one of the translated closed halfspaces contains x because the theta_i S_i weighted margins sum to zero. Hence its exact mass q(t) bounds depth at x, including on the boundaries. At t=0 this normalized bound touches the actual maximum, so its nonzero derivative gives the claimed strict descent.
